overall_narrative_summary: No formal risk-of-bias appraisal could be conducted because the retrieved 15-page PDF contains only Supplemental Material (plus four trailing WHO reference entries on page 1) and completely lacks the main article body (Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion). The supplemental file includes blank data-collection instruments—specifically Part 1a (a bi-monthly questionnaire tracking operational, financial, and institutional Water Safety Plan outcomes alongside water supply continuity, non-revenue water, E. coli/faecal coliforms, turbidity, free residual chlorine, pH, and consumer complaints/satisfaction in Bushenyi-Ishaka) and Part 1b (a quarterly interview guide effective August 2018 probing weather events, disease outbreaks, technology changes, power failures, political events, population/demand shifts, regulatory pressure, budgetary changes, and system challenges)—followed by empty caption headers for Parts 2a and 2b covering July 2018 to March 2021. Because the main Methods and Results sections are missing, it is impossible to verify whether the study uses a comparative quasi-experimental design, a longitudinal mixed-methods single-utility evaluation, or a qualitative/institutional case study, or to evaluate actual sampling, response completeness, measurement execution, confounding adjustment, and selective reporting. All tool and cross-tool risk-of-bias domains are therefore recorded as cannot_tell.

why_tool_chosen: Although marked retrieved_oa_pdf, the provided 15-page text is exclusively the Supplemental Material file rather than the main manuscript. Without the Methods and Results sections, it is not possible to classify the empirical design (e.g., MMAT mixed-methods evaluation vs. ROBINS-I comparative interrupted time series vs. single-case institutional evaluation) or score checklist domains without guessing.
